credit_metrics.text: EBITDA fell by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}} and operating profit by {{operating_profit.change@FY2025}} to {{operating_profit@FY2025}}, so the EBITDA margin narrowed by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}}.

Total debt rose by {{total_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{total_debt@FY2025}} and net debt by {{net_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{net_debt@FY2025}}, taking gross leverage up by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2025}}.

Interest coverage fell by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2025}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2025}}, and FFO to debt by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}} as FFO declined by {{ffo.change@FY2025}} to {{ffo@FY2025}}.

Free cash flow rose by {{fcf.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf@FY2025}}, lifting FCF to debt by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2025}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}}, helped by capex intensity easing by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2025}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2025}}.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments rose by {{cash_like.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_like@FY2025}}, and cash liquidity to revenue rose by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}.

Advance ticket cover rose by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2025}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}}, with contract liabilities up by {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}}, so a larger share of the cash balance is customers' prepayments.
The company renegotiated its Airbus delivery schedule, smoothing deliveries into 2030, and signed a new Pratt & Whitney support agreement covering the costs of grounded aircraft.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2025}} to {{passengers@FY2025}} while capacity was broadly unchanged at {{ask@FY2025}} available seat kilometres, and the load factor improved by {{load_factor.change@FY2025}} to {{load_factor@FY2025}}.

RASK rose by {{rask.change@FY2025}} to {{rask@FY2025}} on a passenger yield of {{passenger_yield@FY2025}}, but CASK rose by {{cask.change@FY2025}} to {{cask@FY2025}}, so unit cost outpaced unit revenue.
The fuel share of costs fell by {{fuel_share_of_costs.change@FY2025}} to {{fuel_share_of_costs@FY2025}}, so the pressure came from non-fuel costs.
The fleet rose by {{fleet.change@FY2025}} to {{fleet@FY2025}} aircraft with an average age of {{fleet_age@FY2025}}, as new A321neo deliveries were partly offset by redeliveries and grounded aircraft.

peer_positioning.text: Wizz Air has the highest EBITDA margin in the low-cost peer group ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2024}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2025}} against a peer median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@2024}}.

Leverage is the weakest in the group: net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2025}} ranks {{net_leverage.peer_rank@2024}} against a peer median of {{net_leverage.peer_median@2024}}, and gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2025}} also ranks {{gross_leverage.peer_rank@2024}}.

Cash generation trails the group: FFO to debt of {{ffo_to_debt@FY2025}} and FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} both rank {{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@2024}} and {{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@2024}} respectively, and interest coverage of {{interest_coverage@FY2025}} ranks {{interest_coverage.peer_rank@2024}}.
Capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} and cash liquidity to revenue of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}} put the company in the middle of the group.

snapshot.text: Wizz Air, the low-cost carrier, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{revenue@FY2025}} in FY2025 while a manufacturer engine recall kept a large part of the fleet grounded and Fitch downgraded the company.
Net leverage rose by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} to {{net_leverage@FY2025}} as EBITDA fell by {{ebitda.change@FY2025}} to {{ebitda@FY2025}}.

The point to watch is unit cost: CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2025}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2025}} while capacity was broadly unchanged, so the earnings base has to carry a heavier debt load.

watch_items.text: Leverage: net leverage of {{net_leverage@FY2025}} is the highest in the peer group ({{net_leverage.peer_rank@2024}}) and rose by {{net_leverage.change@FY2025}} over the year, so deleveraging depends on the earnings recovery.
Unit cost: CASK ex-fuel rose by {{cask_ex_fuel.change@FY2025}} to {{cask_ex_fuel@FY2025}} while capacity was broadly unchanged, the main driver of the weaker margin.

Customer prepayments: advance ticket cover of {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}} is above the peer median of {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_median@2024}} and ranks {{advance_ticket_cover.peer_rank@2024}}, so a larger part of liquidity is refundable if bookings slow.
Grounding: the engine recall kept a large number of aircraft out of service during the year, and the new Pratt & Whitney support agreement covers the direct costs of those aircraft.
